apple-pie.title: Apple pie
apple-pie.text: An apple pie is a fruit pie in which the principal filling is apples. It generally has shortcrust pastry both above and below the filling; the upper pastry may be solid or latticed.

baklava.title: Baklava
baklava.text: Baklava is a layered pastry dessert made of filo pastry, filled with chopped nuts, and sweetened with either syrup or honey.

banh-mi.title: Bánh mì
banh-mi.text: Bánh mì is a renowned Vietnamese staple food. It is a short baguette with thin, crisp crust and a soft, airy texture, usually made with mixed rice flour and wheat flour.

bbq-ribs.title: Spare ribs
bbq-ribs.text: Spare ribs are a variety of ribs cut from the lower portion of a pig, specifically the belly and breastbone, behind the shoulder, and include 11 to 13 long bones. Meat and fat cover the bones.

beef-bolognese.title: Bolognese sauce
beef-bolognese.desc: Main variety of ragù in Italian cuisine
beef-bolognese.text: Bolognese sauce, known in Italian as ragù alla bolognese or ragù bolognese, is the main variety of ragù in Italian cuisine, typical of the city of Bologna.

beef-bourguignon.title: Beef bourguignon
beef-bourguignon.text: Beef bourguignon or bœuf bourguignon, is a French stew of beef braised in red wine, often red Burgundy, and beef stock, typically flavored with carrots, onions, garlic, and a bouquet garni, and garnished with pearl onions and mushrooms.

beef-bulgogi.title: Bulgogi
beef-bulgogi.text: Bulgogi is a gui made of thin, marinated slices of meat, most commonly beef, grilled on a barbecue or on a stove-top griddle. It is also often stir-fried in a pan in home cooking.

bibimbap.title: Bibimbap
bibimbap.text: Bibimbap, sometimes romanised as bi bim bap or bi bim bop, is a Korean rice dish. It is served as a bowl of warm white rice topped with namul and gochujang.

biryani.title: Biryani
biryani.text: Biryani is a mixed rice dish traditionally made with spiced meat, seafood, or vegetables. It was present in Mughal-era India, though whether it was created there is debated.

bouillabaisse.title: Bouillabaisse
bouillabaisse.text: Bouillabaisse is a traditional Provençal fish soup originating in the port city of Marseille. The word is originally a compound of the two Provençal verbs bouillir and baisser.

butter-chicken.title: Butter chicken
butter-chicken.text: Butter chicken or murgh makhani is a curry made from chicken cooked in a spiced tomato and butter-based gravy. The gravy is known for its creamy, rich texture.

buttermilk-pancakes.title: Pancake
buttermilk-pancakes.desc: Thin round cake made of eggs, milk, and flour
buttermilk-pancakes.text: A pancake, also known as a hotcake, griddlecake, or flapjack, is a flat type of batter bread like cake, often thin and round, prepared from a starch-based batter that may contain eggs, milk, and butter, and then cooked on a hot surface such as a griddle or frying pan.

caesar-salad.title: Caesar salad
caesar-salad.desc: Green salad of romaine lettuce and croutons
caesar-salad.text: A Caesar salad, also known as Caesar's salad, is a green salad of romaine lettuce and croutons commonly dressed with lemon juice, olive oil, eggs, Worcestershire sauce, anchovies, garlic, Dijon mustard, Parmesan and black pepper.

photo.artist: Geoff Peters from Vancouver, BC, Canada

caprese-salad.title: Caprese salad
caprese-salad.text: Caprese salad is an Italian salad composed of sliced fresh mozzarella, tomatoes, and basil, seasoned with salt and olive oil or balsamic vinegar. The salad's name references the island of Capri, where it is believed to have originated.

chana-masala.title: Chana masala
chana-masala.desc: Chickpea dish from the Indian subcontinent
chana-masala.text: Chana masala is a chickpea curry cooked in a tomato-based sauce, originating from the Indian subcontinent. It is a staple dish in Indian and Pakistani cuisine.

photo.artist: Simon Law (sfllaw) from Montréal, QC, Canada

cheeseburger.title: Cheeseburger
cheeseburger.text: A cheeseburger is a hamburger with melted cheese on top of the meat patty, added near the end of the cooking time. Cheeseburgers can include variations in structure, ingredients and composition.

chicken-enchiladas.title: Enchilada
chicken-enchiladas.desc: Corn tortilla rolled around a filling and covered with a sauce
chicken-enchiladas.text: An enchilada is a Mexican dish consisting of a corn tortilla rolled around a filling and covered with a savory sauce. Enchiladas can be filled with various ingredients, including meats, cheese, beans, potatoes, vegetables, or combinations.

chicken-gumbo.title: Gumbo
chicken-gumbo.text: Gumbo is a stew that is popular among the U.S. Gulf Coast community, the New Orleans stew variation being the official state cuisine of the U.S. state of Louisiana.

chicken-satay.title: Satay
chicken-satay.text: Satay or sate is a Southeast Asian dish consisting of small pieces of seasoned meat, seafood or vegetables skewered on sticks and grilled over charcoal. It is typically served with a sauce, most commonly peanut-based and accompanied by rice cakes, cucumber or pickled vegetables.

chicken-shawarma.title: Shawarma
chicken-shawarma.text: Shawarma is a Middle Eastern food that originated in the Levant during the Ottoman Empire. It consists of meat cut into thin slices, stacked in an inverted cone, and roasted on a slow-turning vertical spit.

chicken-tikka.title: Chicken tikka masala
chicken-tikka.text: Chicken tikka masala is a curry consisting of roasted marinated chicken pieces in a creamy spiced sauce (masala). It is thought to have been created in Britain, possibly by Ali Ahmed Aslam in Glasgow.

chiles-rellenos.title: Chile relleno
chiles-rellenos.desc: Stuffed chili pepper dish in Mexican cuisine
chiles-rellenos.text: The chile relleno is a dish in Mexican cuisine. In 1858, it was described as a "green chile pepper stuffed with minced meat and coated with eggs".

chocolate-chip-cookies.title: Chocolate chip cookie
chocolate-chip-cookies.text: A chocolate chip cookie is a drop cookie that contains pieces of chocolate mixed into the dough before baking. Texture and appearance vary with ingredients and preparation, ranging from moist, chewy cookies to ones that are crispy.

churros.title: Churro
churros.text: A churro is a type of fried dough from Spanish and Portuguese cuisine, made with choux pastry dough piped into hot oil with a piping bag and large closed star tip or similar shape.

clam-chowder.title: Clam chowder
clam-chowder.desc: Soup containing clams and broth or milk
clam-chowder.text: Clam chowder is any of several chowder soups in American cuisine containing clams. In addition to clams, common ingredients include diced potatoes, salt pork, and onions.

coq-au-vin.title: Coq au vin
coq-au-vin.text: Coq au vin is a French dish of chicken braised with wine, lardons, mushrooms, and optionally garlic.

photo.artist: Beck from East Midlands, United Kingdon

creme-brulee.title: Crème brûlée
creme-brulee.desc: Custard dessert with hard caramel top
creme-brulee.text: Crème brûlée, also known as burnt cream, Cambridge burnt cream, or Trinity cream, and virtually identical to crema catalana, is a dessert consisting of a rich custard base topped with a layer of hardened caramelized sugar.

croissant.title: Croissant
croissant.text: A croissant is a Viennoiserie in a crescent shape made from a laminated yeast dough that sits between a bread and a puff pastry.

dal-tadka.title: Dal
dal-tadka.desc: Dried, split pulses used for cooking
dal-tadka.text: Dal are dried, split pulses that can require soaking before cooking. India is the largest producer of pulses in the world.

falafel.title: Falafel
falafel.text: Falafel is a deep-fried ball or patty-shaped fritter of Egyptian origin that features in Middle Eastern cuisine, particularly Levantine cuisines. It is made from ground fava beans, chickpeas, or both, and mixed with herbs and spices before frying.

french-onion-soup.title: French onion soup
french-onion-soup.text: French onion soup is a soup of onions which are sautéed and then cooked in meat stock or water, usually served gratinéed with croutons or a larger piece of bread covered with cheese floating on top.

fried-chicken.title: Fried chicken
fried-chicken.desc: Dish of seasoned chicken pieces that are coated and fried
fried-chicken.text: Fried chicken, more formally known as Southern fried chicken, is a dish consisting of chicken pieces, coated with seasoned flour or batter, that are pan-fried, deep-fried, pressure-fried, or air-fried.

garlic-naan.title: Naan
garlic-naan.text: Naan is a leavened, oven-baked or tawa-fried flatbread, that can also be baked in a tandoor. It is characterised by a light and fluffy texture and golden-brown spots from the baking process.

gazpacho.title: Gazpacho
gazpacho.text: Gazpacho or gaspacho, also called Andalusian gazpacho, is a cold soup and drink made of raw, blended vegetables. It originated in the southern regions of the Iberian Peninsula and spread into other areas.

greek-salad.title: Greek salad
greek-salad.desc: Salad of tomatoes, cucumbers, and feta
greek-salad.text: Greek salad, choriatiki or Horiatiki is a salad in Greek cuisine generally made with pieces of tomatoes, cucumbers, onion, feta cheese, and olives and dressed with salt, Greek oregano, and olive oil.

guacamole.title: Guacamole
guacamole.text: Guacamole, sometimes informally shortened to guac in the United States, is an avocado-based dip, spread, or salad first developed in Mexico. In addition to its use in modern Mexican cuisine, it has become part of international cuisine as a dip, condiment, and salad ingredient.

hummus.title: Hummus
hummus.text: Hummus is a Levantine dip, spread, or savory dish made from cooked, mashed chickpeas blended with tahini, lemon juice, and garlic. The standard garnish includes olive oil, a few whole chickpeas, parsley, and paprika.

kung-pao-chicken.title: Kung Pao chicken
kung-pao-chicken.text: Kung Pao chicken, also transcribed Gong Bao or Kung Po, is a spicy, stir-fried Chinese dish made with cubes of cooked chicken, peanuts, vegetables and chili peppers, and Sichuan peppercorns.

laksa.title: Laksa
laksa.desc: Spicy noodle dish from Southeast Asia
laksa.text: Laksa is a spicy noodle dish popular in Southeast Asia. Laksa consists of various types of noodles, most commonly thick rice noodles, with toppings such as chicken, prawns or fish.

lamb-kofta.title: Kofta
lamb-kofta.desc: Middle Eastern and South Asian meatballs
lamb-kofta.text: Kofta is a family of meatball and meatloaf dishes found in South Asian, Central Asian, Balkan, Middle Eastern, North African, and South Caucasian cuisines.

lasagna.title: Lasagna
lasagna.desc: Flat pasta and stacked pasta dishes
lasagna.text: Lasagna, also known by the plural form lasagne, is a type of pasta made in wide, flat sheets.

linguine-vongole.title: Spaghetti alle vongole
linguine-vongole.text: Spaghetti alle vongole is a pasta dish consisting of spaghetti cooked with fresh clams, originating in the coastal regions of Italy, particularly in southern Italy. The preparation typically involves garlic, parsley, olive oil, and occasionally white wine.

mac-and-cheese.title: Macaroni and cheese
mac-and-cheese.text: Macaroni and cheese is a pasta dish of macaroni covered in cheese sauce, most commonly cheddar sauce. Its origins trace back to cheese and pasta casseroles in medieval England.

mapo-tofu.title: Mapo tofu
mapo-tofu.text: Mapo tofu is a popular Chinese dish from Sichuan province. It consists of tofu set in a spicy sauce, typically a thin, oily, and bright red suspension, based on douban, and douchi, along with minced meat, traditionally beef.

margherita-pizza.title: Pizza Margherita
margherita-pizza.text: Pizza Margherita, also known as Margherita pizza, is, together with the pizza marinara, the typical Neapolitan pizza. It is roundish in shape with a raised edge and seasoned with hand-crushed peeled tomatoes, mozzarella, fresh basil leaves, and extra virgin olive oil.

miso-ramen.title: Ramen
miso-ramen.text: Ramen is a Japanese-Chinese fusion noodle dish. It includes Chinese-style alkaline wheat noodles served in several flavors of hot broth.

miso-soup.title: Miso soup
miso-soup.text: Miso soup is a traditional Japanese soup consisting of miso in a dashi stock. It is commonly served as part of an ichijū-sansai (一汁三菜) meal 'one soup, three dishes' consisting of rice, soup, and side dishes.

mole-poblano.title: Mole (sauce)
mole-poblano.text: Mole or mōlli is a traditional sauce and marinade originally used in Mexican cuisine. In contemporary Mexico, the term is used for numerous sauces, including some fifty distinct varieties of mole across Mexico.

moussaka.title: Moussaka
moussaka.desc: Dish of layered vegetables, sauce and meat
moussaka.text: Moussaka is an aubergine (eggplant)- or potato-based dish, often including ground meat, which is common in the Balkans and the Middle East, with many local and regional variations.

mujadara.title: Mujaddara
mujadara.desc: Dish of lentils, rice and sautéed onions
mujadara.text: Mujaddara is a dish consisting of cooked lentils together with groats, generally rice, and garnished with sautéed onions. It is especially popular in the Levant.

osso-buco.title: Ossobuco
osso-buco.text: Ossobuco or osso buco, also known as ossobuco alla milanese, is a specialty of Lombard cuisine of cross-cut veal shanks braised with vegetables, white wine, and broth.

pad-thai.title: Pad thai
pad-thai.text: Pad thai is a stir-fried rice noodle dish commonly served as a street food in Thailand as part of Thai cuisine. It is typically made with rice noodles, shrimp, peanuts, green onions, scrambled egg, sugar and bean sprouts.

paella.title: Paella
paella.desc: Rice dish from the Valencian Community, Spain
paella.text: Paella is a rice dish originally from the Valencian Community. Paella is regarded as one of the community's identifying symbols.

palak-paneer.title: Palak paneer
palak-paneer.text: Palak paneer or palak chhena is a dish from the Indian subcontinent consisting of chhena or paneer in a thick paste made from puréed spinach, called palak in Hindi, Marathi, Gujarati, Punjabi and other Indian languages.

panna-cotta.title: Panna cotta
panna-cotta.desc: Italian dessert of cream and gelatin
panna-cotta.text: Panna cotta is an Italian dessert of sweetened cream thickened with gelatin and moulded. It may be flavoured with coffee, vanilla, or other flavours.

patatas-bravas.title: Patatas bravas
patatas-bravas.text: Patatas bravas is a dish native to Spain. It typically consists of white potatoes that have been cut into two-centimeter-wide cubes, then fried in oil and served hot with a spicy "brava" sauce.

pesto-genovese.title: Pesto
pesto-genovese.text: Pesto, also known as pesto genovese, is an Italian paste traditionally made with leaves of Genovese basil, extra virgin olive oil, Parmesan, pecorino sardo, pine nuts, and garlic. It originated in the Ligurian city of Genoa and is used to dress pasta.

pho.title: Pho
pho.text: Pho is a Vietnamese soup dish consisting of broth, rice noodles, herbs, and meat – usually beef, and sometimes chicken. Pho is a popular food in Vietnam where it is served in households, street-stalls, and restaurants nationwide.

pork-gyoza.title: Jiaozi
pork-gyoza.text: Jiaozi are a type of Chinese dumpling. They typically consist of a ground meat or vegetable filling wrapped into a thinly rolled piece of dough, which is then sealed by pressing the edges together.

pork-souvlaki.title: Souvlaki
pork-souvlaki.text: Souvlaki is a Greek food consisting of small pieces of meat and sometimes vegetables grilled on a skewer. It is usually eaten straight off the skewer while still hot.

pozole-rojo.title: Pozole
pozole-rojo.text: Pozole is a traditional soup or stew from Mexican cuisine. It is made from hominy with meat, and can be seasoned and garnished with shredded lettuce or cabbage, chili peppers, onion, garlic, radishes, avocado, salsa or limes.

quiche-lorraine.title: Quiche Lorraine
quiche-lorraine.desc: Savoury open pastry tart with a filling of egg, cream and bacon
quiche-lorraine.text: Quiche Lorraine is a savoury French tart with a filling of cream, eggs, and bacon, in an open pastry case. It was little known outside the French region of Lorraine until the mid-20th century.

ratatouille.title: Ratatouille
ratatouille.text: Ratatouille is a traditional French vegetable dish originating in the Provence region of southern France, particularly associated with Nice and its surrounding region.

risotto-saffron.title: Risotto
risotto-saffron.text: Risotto is an Italian rice dish cooked with broth until it reaches a creamy consistency. The broth can be derived from meat, fish or vegetables.

salade-nicoise.title: Salade niçoise
salade-nicoise.desc: French salad with anchovies or tuna
salade-nicoise.text: Salade niçoise is a salad that originated in the French city of Nice. It is traditionally made of tomatoes, hard-boiled eggs, Niçoise olives and anchovies or tuna, dressed with olive oil or, in some historical versions, a vinaigrette.

samosa.title: Samosa
samosa.text: A samosa or shingara is a fried Indian subcontinent turnover with a savoury filling that mostly consists of vegetables like spiced potatoes, onions, and peas, but can include cheese such as paneer, meat or even fish. Its name originates from the Middle Persian word sambosag (سنبوسگ).

shakshuka.title: Shakshouka
shakshuka.desc: Maghrebi dish of eggs poached in a sauce
shakshuka.text: Shakshouka is a Maghrebi dish of eggs poached in a sauce of tomatoes, olive oil, peppers, onion, and garlic, commonly spiced with cumin, paprika, and cayenne pepper. Shakshouka is a popular dish throughout North Africa and the Middle East.

shrimp-ceviche.title: Ceviche
shrimp-ceviche.text: Ceviche, cebiche, sebiche, or seviche is a traditional cold dish consisting of raw fish or shellfish marinated in citrus and seasonings.

som-tam.title: Green papaya salad
som-tam.desc: Spicy salad made from unripe papaya
som-tam.text: Green papaya salad is a spicy salad made from shredded unripe papaya. It is believed to have been created by Lao people and is considered one of the national dishes of Laos.

spaghetti-carbonara.title: Carbonara
spaghetti-carbonara.text: Carbonara is a pasta dish made with cured pork, hard cheese, eggs, salt, and black pepper. It is typical of the Lazio region of Italy.

spanakopita.title: Savory spinach pie
spanakopita.desc: Savory spinach pie made with filo pastry
spanakopita.text: Savory spinach pie is a pastry eaten throughout Greece, Bosnia and Herzegovina, and Turkey. Of Greek origin, this pastry’s filling is made with chopped spinach and usually feta or white cheese, and egg.

sushi-roll.title: Sushi
sushi-roll.text: Sushi is a traditional Japanese dish made with vinegared rice, typically seasoned with sugar and salt, and combined with a variety of ingredients, such as seafood, vegetables, or meat; raw seafood is the most common, although some may be cooked.

tabbouleh.title: Tabbouleh
tabbouleh.desc: Levantine dish of parsley and bulgur
tabbouleh.text: Tabbouleh, also transcribed tabouleh, tabbouli, tabouli, or taboulah, is a Levantine salad of finely chopped parsley, bulgur, tomato, mint, and onion, seasoned with olive oil, lemon juice, salt and sometimes sweet pepper. Some variations add lettuce, or use semolina instead of bulgur.

tacos-al-pastor.title: Al pastor
tacos-al-pastor.desc: Mexican spit-grilled pork seasoned with adobada
tacos-al-pastor.text: Al pastor, tacos al pastor, or tacos de trompo is a preparation of sliced, spit-grilled meat, usually pork, originating in the Central Mexican region of Puebla where they remain most prominent, though it is a common menu item found in taquerías throughout Mexico.

tarte-tatin.title: Tarte Tatin
tarte-tatin.text: The tarte Tatin is a tart in which the fruit is caramelized in butter and sugar before the tart is baked. Named after the Tatin sisters who invented it and served it in their hotel as its signature dish, it originated in France but has spread to other countries over time.

teriyaki-salmon.title: Teriyaki
teriyaki-salmon.text: Teriyaki is a cooking technique in which foods are broiled or grilled with a glaze of soy sauce, mirin, and sugar.

thai-green-curry.title: Green curry
thai-green-curry.text: Green curry is a variety of curry originating from central Thailand.

tiramisu.title: Tiramisu
tiramisu.text: Tiramisu is an Italian dessert made with coffee-soaked ladyfingers covered with a cream of egg yolks, sugar, mascarpone, and cocoa powder. It originated in northeastern Italy, and modern versions were popularized in restaurants from the 1970s.

tom-yum.title: Tom yum
tom-yum.text: Tom yum or tom yam is a family of hot and sour Thai soups. The name tom yam is composed of two words in the Thai language: tom refers to the boiling process, while yam means "mixed".

Adobo Sauce.title: Adobo
Adobo Sauce.text: Adobo or adobar is the immersion of food in a stock composed variously of paprika, oregano, salt, garlic, and vinegar to preserve and enhance its flavor. The Portuguese variant is known as carne de vinha d'alhos.

Ají Amarillo Sauce.title: Ají (sauce)
Ají Amarillo Sauce.text: Ají is a spicy sauce that contains ají peppers, oil, tomatoes, cilantro (coriander), garlic, onions, and water. It is served as a condiment to complement main dishes popular in Latin American cuisines, and prepared by blending its ingredients using a food processor or blender.

Aji Sauce.title: Ají (sauce)
Aji Sauce.text: Ají is a spicy sauce that contains ají peppers, oil, tomatoes, cilantro (coriander), garlic, onions, and water. It is served as a condiment to complement main dishes popular in Latin American cuisines, and prepared by blending its ingredients using a food processor or blender.

Alfredo.title: Fettuccine Alfredo
Alfredo.desc: Creamy pasta dish with butter and cheese
Alfredo.text: Fettuccine Alfredo is a pasta dish consisting of fettuccine tossed with butter and Parmesan cheese which is melted and emulsified to form a rich cheese sauce coating the pasta. Originating in Rome in the early 20th century, the recipe is now known primarily in the United States and other countries.

Allemande.title: Allemande sauce
Allemande.desc: Sauce used in classic French cuisine
Allemande.text: Allemande sauce or sauce parisienne is a sauce in French cuisine based on a light-colored velouté sauce, but thickened with egg yolks and heavy cream, and seasoned with lemon juice.

photo.artist: Alex Kane from New York, USA

Arrabbiata.title: Arrabbiata sauce
Arrabbiata.text: Arrabbiata sauce, known in Italian as arrabbiata, is a spicy sauce made with tomatoes, garlic, peperoncino, parsley, and extra virgin olive oil. The sauce originates from the Lazio region of Italy, and particularly from the city of Rome.

BBQ Sauce.title: Barbecue sauce
BBQ Sauce.desc: Sauce used as a marinade, basting, or topping
BBQ Sauce.text: Barbecue sauce is a sauce used as a marinade, basting, or topping for meat cooked in the barbecue cooking style, including pork, beef, and chicken. It is a ubiquitous condiment in the Southern United States and Australia which is used on many other foods as well.

Béarnaise.title: Béarnaise sauce
Béarnaise.desc: Sauce made of clarified butter and egg yolk
Béarnaise.text: Béarnaise sauce is a sauce made of clarified butter, egg yolk, white wine vinegar, and herbs. It is regarded as a "child" of hollandaise sauce.

Béchamel.title: Béchamel sauce
Béchamel.desc: French white sauce based on roux and milk
Béchamel.text: Béchamel sauce is a white sauce made from a roux of butter and flour, heated in cream or milk, and seasoned with ground nutmeg. Béchamel is one of the mother sauces of French cuisine.

Berbere Sauce.title: Berbere
Berbere Sauce.text: Berbere is a spice mixture whose constituent elements usually include chili peppers, coriander, garlic, ginger, Ethiopian holy basil (besobela) seeds, korarima, rue, ajwain or radhuni, nigella, and fenugreek. It is a key ingredient in the cuisines of Ethiopia and Eritrea.

Bercy.title: Sauce bercy
Bercy.text: Sauce Bercy is a classic sauce of French cuisine. The main ingredients are fish stock, velouté sauce, white wine, shallots and butter.

Beurre Blanc.title: Beurre blanc
Beurre Blanc.text: Beurre blanc or beurre Nantais is a warm emulsified butter sauce made with a reduction of vinegar, lemon juice and/or white wine and shallots into which cold whole butter is slowly added and whisked.

photo.artist: Eric Lin from San Francisco, USA

Beurre Noisette.title: Beurre noisette
Beurre Noisette.text: Beurre noisette is a type of warm sauce used in French cuisine. It can accompany savoury foods, such as winter vegetables, pasta, fish, omelettes, and chicken.

Bolognese.title: Bolognese sauce
Bolognese.desc: Main variety of ragù in Italian cuisine
Bolognese.text: Bolognese sauce, known in Italian as ragù alla bolognese or ragù bolognese, is the main variety of ragù in Italian cuisine, typical of the city of Bologna.

Bordelaise.title: Bordelaise sauce
Bordelaise.text: Bordelaise sauce is a classic French sauce named after the Bordeaux region of France, which is famous for its wine. According to Auguste Escoffier in his book Ma cuisine, sauce bordelaise is made using white wine.

Buffalo Sauce.title: Buffalo wing
Buffalo Sauce.desc: American dish of spicy chicken wings
Buffalo Sauce.text: A Buffalo wing in American cuisine is an unbreaded chicken wing section that is generally deep-fried, then coated or dipped in a sauce consisting of a vinegar-based cayenne pepper hot sauce and melted butter.

Bulgogi Marinade.title: Bulgogi
Bulgogi Marinade.text: Bulgogi is a gui made of thin, marinated slices of meat, most commonly beef, grilled on a barbecue or on a stove-top griddle. It is also often stir-fried in a pan in home cooking.

Chasseur.title: Chasseur (sauce)
Chasseur.text: Sauce chasseur is a brown sauce used in French cuisine. It is typically made using demi-glace or espagnole sauce as a base, and includes mushrooms and shallots or onions.

Cheddar Sauce.title: Cheddar sauce
Cheddar Sauce.desc: British sauce made with cheddar cheese
Cheddar Sauce.text: Cheddar sauce, cheddar cheese sauce, or cheese sauce is a traditional sauce used in English cooking. The sauce is based upon Béchamel (white) sauce, which is known as one of the 'mother sauces', and cheddar cheese.

photo.artist: Stuart Spivack from Cleveland, Ohio, USA

Chermoula.title: Chermoula
Chermoula.text: Chermoula or charmoula is a marinade and relish used in Algerian, Libyan, Moroccan and Tunisian cooking. It is traditionally used to flavor fish or seafood, but it can be used on other meats or vegetables.

Chimichurri.title: Chimichurri
Chimichurri.text: Chimichurri is an uncooked sauce used as an ingredient in cooking and as a table condiment for grilled meat. Found originally in Argentina and used in Argentine, Uruguayan, Paraguayan and Brazilian cuisines, it has become widely adopted in most of Latin America.

Chimichurri Verde.title: Chimichurri
Chimichurri Verde.text: Chimichurri is an uncooked sauce used as an ingredient in cooking and as a table condiment for grilled meat. Found originally in Argentina and used in Argentine, Uruguayan, Paraguayan and Brazilian cuisines, it has become widely adopted in most of Latin America.

Dashi.title: Dashi
Dashi.desc: Family of stocks used in Japanese cuisine
Dashi.text: Dashi is a family of stocks used in Japanese cuisine. Dashi forms the base for miso soup, clear broth soup, noodle broth soup, and many simmering liquids to accentuate the savory flavor known as umami.

Demi-glace.title: Demi-glace
Demi-glace.text: Demi-glace is a rich brown sauce in French cuisine used by itself or as a base for other sauces. The term comes from the French word glace, which, when used in reference to a sauce, means "icing" or "glaze".

Espagnole.title: Espagnole sauce
Espagnole.text: Espagnole sauce is a basic brown sauce, and is one of the mother sauces of classic French cuisine. It is a strong-flavoured brown sauce, made from a dark brown roux and brown stock—usually beef or veal stock—and tomatoes or tomato paste.

Gastrique.title: Gastrique
Gastrique.text: Gastrique is caramelized sugar, deglazed with vinegar or other sour liquids, used as a sweet and sour flavoring for sauces.

Gochujang Sauce.title: Gochujang
Gochujang Sauce.text: Gochujang or red chili paste is a savory, sweet, and spicy fermented condiment popular in Korean cooking. It is made from gochugaru, chapssal, meju powder, yeotgireum, and salt.

Gravy (Southern).title: Gravy
Gravy (Southern).desc: Sauce made from the juices of meats
Gravy (Southern).text: Gravy is a sauce made from the juices of meats and vegetables that run naturally during cooking and often thickened with thickeners for added texture. The gravy may be further coloured and flavoured with gravy salt, gravy browning, or bouillon cubes.

Groundnut Sauce.title: Peanut stew
Groundnut Sauce.text: Peanut stew or groundnut stew, also known as maafe, and pate d'arachide (French), is a staple food stew in Western Africa.

Harissa.title: Harissa
Harissa.text: Harissa is a Tunisian hot chili pepper paste. Peppers in the country were first grown in the Cape Bon Peninsula, birthplace of the condiment, with Nabeul famous for being the primary center for its production.

Hollandaise.title: Hollandaise sauce
Hollandaise.desc: Sauce made of egg, butter, and lemon
Hollandaise.text: Hollandaise sauce is a French recipe, a mixture of egg yolk, melted butter, and lemon juice. It is usually seasoned with salt, and either white pepper or cayenne pepper.

Korma.title: Korma
Korma.text: Korma, kurma, qorma or qurma is a curry dish originating in the Indian subcontinent influenced by Mughlai cuisine, versions of which later were modified to Anglo-Indian and then to British tastes.

Kung Pao.title: Kung Pao chicken
Kung Pao.text: Kung Pao chicken, also transcribed Gong Bao or Kung Po, is a spicy, stir-fried Chinese dish made with cubes of cooked chicken, peanuts, vegetables and chili peppers, and Sichuan peppercorns.

Makhani (Butter Chicken).title: Butter chicken
Makhani (Butter Chicken).text: Butter chicken or murgh makhani is a curry made from chicken cooked in a spiced tomato and butter-based gravy. The gravy is known for its creamy, rich texture.

Mango Chutney.title: Green mango chutney
Mango Chutney.desc: Indian chutney made from unripe mangoes
Mango Chutney.text: Green mango chutney, also known as raw mango chutney, is an Indian chutney prepared from unripe mangoes. Ripe mangoes are sweet and are not used for chutneys as they are eaten raw.

Marinara.title: Marinara sauce
Marinara.text: Marinara sauce is a tomato sauce usually made with tomatoes, garlic, herbs, and onions. Variations include capers, olives, spices, and a dash of wine.

Mint Chutney.title: Chutney
Mint Chutney.text: A chutney is a condiment associated with cuisines of the Indian subcontinent. Chutneys are made in a wide variety of forms, some raw such as with coriander, others cooked with sugar, like mango chutney.

Mole Negro.title: Mole (sauce)
Mole Negro.text: Mole or mōlli is a traditional sauce and marinade originally used in Mexican cuisine. In contemporary Mexico, the term is used for numerous sauces, including some fifty distinct varieties of mole across Mexico.

Mole Poblano.title: Mole (sauce)
Mole Poblano.text: Mole or mōlli is a traditional sauce and marinade originally used in Mexican cuisine. In contemporary Mexico, the term is used for numerous sauces, including some fifty distinct varieties of mole across Mexico.

Mornay.title: Mornay sauce
Mornay.desc: Type of béchamel sauce including cheese
Mornay.text: A Mornay sauce is a béchamel sauce with grated cheese added. The usual cheeses in French cuisine are Parmesan and Gruyère, but other cheeses may also be used.

Nuoc Cham.title: Nước chấm
Nuoc Cham.text: Nước chấm, or more specifically nước mắm chấm for the fish-sauce version, is a Vietnamese dipping sauce often served as a condiment. It is a sweet, sour, salty, savoury sauce that often contains bird's eye chili for spiciness.

Pad Thai Sauce.title: Pad thai
Pad Thai Sauce.text: Pad thai is a stir-fried rice noodle dish commonly served as a street food in Thailand as part of Thai cuisine. It is typically made with rice noodles, shrimp, peanuts, green onions, scrambled egg, sugar and bean sprouts.

Peanut Sauce (Thai).title: Peanut sauce
Peanut Sauce (Thai).desc: Indonesian sauce made from ground roasted or fried peanuts
Peanut Sauce (Thai).text: In Indonesian cuisine, peanut sauce is a sauce made from ground roasted or fried peanuts, widely used in and many other dishes throughout the world. Specific versions of this sauce include satay sauce, pecel sauce, and sambal kacang, the satay having been adapted globally.

Ponzu.title: Ponzu
Ponzu.text: Ponzu (ポン酢) is a citrus-based sauce commonly used in Japanese cuisine. It is tart, with a thin, watery consistency.

Puttanesca.title: Spaghetti alla puttanesca
Puttanesca.text: Spaghetti alla puttanesca is a pasta dish invented in the Italian city of Naples in the mid-20th century, typically made with tomatoes, olives, capers, anchovies, garlic, peperoncino, and extra virgin olive oil.

Raita.title: Raita
Raita.text: Raita is a side dish and condiment in Indian cuisine made of dahi together with raw or cooked vegetables, fruit, or pulses. The yogurt may be seasoned with herbs and spices such as coriander, roasted cumin seeds, mint, and cayenne pepper.

Remoulade.title: Remoulade
Remoulade.text: Remoulade is a cold sauce. Although similar to tartar sauce, it is often more yellowish, sometimes flavored with curry, and often contains chopped pickles or piccalilli.

Robert.title: Sauce Robert
Robert.text: Sauce Robert is a brown mustard sauce and one of the small sauces, or compound sauces, derived from the classic French demi-glace, which in turn is derived from espagnole sauce, one of the five mother sauces in French cuisine.

Romesco.title: Romesco
Romesco.desc: Catalan sauce of tomatoes, garlic, and nuts
Romesco.text: Romesco is a tomato-based sauce that originated from Valls in Catalonia. The fishermen in this area made this sauce to be eaten with fish.

Saag.title: Saag
Saag.desc: Leafy vegetable dish from the Indian subcontinent
Saag.text: Saag, also spelled sag, saagh, saga, shaak or shak, is a leafy vegetable dish from the Indian subcontinent. It is eaten with bread, such as roti or naan, or in some regions with rice.

Salsa Macha.title: Salsa macha
Salsa Macha.text: Salsa macha is a Mexican spicy condiment typically made of vegetable oil, dried chilies, garlic and salt. The chilies may be chile de árbol, serrano, chipotle, pequin or morita.

Salsa Roja.title: Salsa (food)
Salsa Roja.text: A salsa is any of a variety of sauces used as condiments for tacos and other Mexican and Mexican-American foods, and as dips for tortilla chips. They may be raw or cooked, and are generally served at room temperature.

Salsa Verde.title: Salsa verde
Salsa Verde.desc: Spicy Mexican sauce made from tomatillos
Salsa Verde.text: In Mexican cuisine, salsa verde is a spicy green sauce made from tomatillo and green chili peppers. It dates to the Aztec Empire, as documented by the Spanish physician Francisco Hernández, and is distinct from the various medieval European parsley-based green sauces.

Shito.title: Shito
Shito.text: Shito or shitor din is a hot black pepper sauce ubiquitous in Ghanaian cuisine. The name comes from the Ga language.

Sofrito.title: Sofrito
Sofrito.text: Sofrito, sofregit, soffritto, sofrit, refogado or sueztitze typically consists of aromatic ingredients cut into small pieces and sautéed or braised in cooking oil for a long period of time over low heat, then used as a foundation for a variety of dishes.

Soubise.title: Soubise sauce
Soubise.text: Soubise sauce is an onion sauce thickened with béchamel sauce, pounded cooked rice, or cream. It is generally served with meats, game, poultry and vegetables.

Suprême.title: Suprême sauce
Suprême.text: Suprême sauce is a classic and popular "daughter sauce" of French cuisine. It consists of velouté, a "mother sauce", thickened with cream and strained.

Sweet and Sour Sauce.title: Sweet and sour
Sweet and Sour Sauce.text: Sweet and sour is a generic term that encompasses many styles of sauce, cuisine, and cooking methods common to Eurasia. Sweet and sour sauce has remained popular in Asian and Western cuisines since the Middle Ages.

Tahini Sauce.title: Tahini
Tahini Sauce.desc: Middle Eastern condiment made from sesame
Tahini Sauce.text: Tahini is a Middle Eastern condiment made from ground sesame seeds. The most common variety comes from hulled seeds, but unhulled ones can also be used; the latter variety is slightly bitter, but more nutritious.

Tare.title: Tare sauce
Tare.text: Tare, or tare sauce, is a type of dipping sauce used in Japanese cuisine. The sauce is best described as sweetened, thickened soy sauce for grilling and flavored soy sauce with dashi, vinegar, etc., for nabemono and nattō such as ponzu but every chef has their own variation.

Teriyaki.title: Teriyaki
Teriyaki.text: Teriyaki is a cooking technique in which foods are broiled or grilled with a glaze of soy sauce, mirin, and sugar.

Thai Green Curry.title: Green curry
Thai Green Curry.text: Green curry is a variety of curry originating from central Thailand.

Thai Red Curry.title: Red curry
Thai Red Curry.text: Red curry is a Thai dish consisting of red curry paste cooked in coconut milk with meat such as chicken, beef, pork, duck or shrimp added, or else a vegetarian protein source such as tofu.

Tikka Masala.title: Chicken tikka masala
Tikka Masala.text: Chicken tikka masala is a curry consisting of roasted marinated chicken pieces in a creamy spiced sauce (masala). It is thought to have been created in Britain, possibly by Ali Ahmed Aslam in Glasgow.

Tomato Sauce (Classic French).title: Tomato sauce
Tomato Sauce (Classic French).text: Tomato sauce can refer to many different sauces made primarily from tomatoes. In some countries the term refers to a sauce to be served as part of a dish; in others, it is a condiment.

Tonkatsu Sauce.title: Tonkatsu sauce
Tonkatsu Sauce.text: Tonkatsu sauce or katsu sauce is a Japanese sauce served with tonkatsu. It is a thick Japanese Worcestershire-type sauce.

Toum.title: Toum
Toum.desc: Garlic sauce common in the Levant
Toum.text: Salsat toum, also known as toumiya or simply toum, is a garlic sauce common to the Levant. It is similar to the Provençal aioli.

Velouté.title: Velouté sauce
Velouté.desc: French sauce made from roux and light stock
Velouté.text: A velouté sauce is a savory sauce that is made from a roux and a light stock. It is one of the "mother sauces" of French cuisine listed by chef Auguste Escoffier in the early twentieth century.

Vindaloo.title: Vindaloo
Vindaloo.text: Vindaloo is a curry dish known globally in its British form as a staple of curry houses and Indian restaurants, specifically a fiery, spicy dish that can be made with a choice of meats. Vindaloo's name derives from the famous Portuguese Goan dish carne de vinha d'alhos or vindalho, made with pork.

XO Sauce.title: XO sauce
XO Sauce.desc: Spicy seafood sauce from Hong Kong
XO Sauce.text: XO sauce is a spicy seafood sauce from Hong Kong with an umami flavour. It is commonly used in southern Chinese regions such as Guangdong.

Yangnyeom.title: Yangnyeom chicken
Yangnyeom.text: Yangnyeom chicken is a variety of Korean fried chicken seasoned with a sweet and spicy sauce of gochujang, garlic, sugar, and other spices. It is often eaten as anju, food consumed while drinking, in South Korea.

Zhug.title: Zhug
Zhug.text: Zhug, also known as sahawiq, is a hot sauce originating in Yemeni cuisine. In other countries of the Arabian Peninsula it is also called mabooj, and bisbaas.

20th Century.title: 20th century (cocktail)
20th Century.desc: Cocktail of gin, Kina Lillet and creme de cacao
20th Century.text: The 20th century is a cocktail created in 1937 by a British bartender named C.A. Tuck, and named in honor of the celebrated 20th Century Limited train which ran between New York City and Chicago from 1902 until 1967.

Alexander.title: Alexander (cocktail)
Alexander.desc: Cocktail of cognac, chocolate liqueur and cream
Alexander.text: The Alexander is a cocktail consisting of cognac, crème de cacao, and cream. It dates from the early 20th century.

Amaretto Sour.title: Amaretto sour
Amaretto Sour.text: An amaretto sour is a cocktail using amaretto liqueur. It is a type of sour, a mixed drink made with a base spirit, citrus juice, and a sweetener.

Americano.title: Americano (cocktail)
Americano.desc: Cocktail composed of Campari, sweet vermouth, and club soda
Americano.text: The Americano is an IBA official cocktail composed of Campari, sweet vermouth and, for the sparkling version, club soda and garnished with a slice of lemon or an orange twist.

Angel Face.title: Angel face (cocktail)
Angel Face.text: The angel face is a cocktail made from gin, apricot brandy and Calvados in equal amounts.

photo.artist: Michael Styne from Averill Park, NY, USA

Aperol Spritz.title: Spritz (cocktail)
Aperol Spritz.text: A spritz is an Italian wine-based cocktail, commonly served as an apéritif across Italy. It consists of Prosecco, a mixer, and a flavouring ingredient, which can be a bitter liqueur, a bitter apéritif, an amaro or a syrup.

Aviation.title: Aviation (cocktail)
Aviation.text: The aviation is a cocktail made with gin, maraschino liqueur, crème de violette and lemon juice. Some recipes omit the crème de violette.

B-52.title: B-52 (cocktail)
B-52.desc: Cocktail of coffee liqueur, Irish cream, and orange-flavored liqueur
B-52.text: The B-52 cocktail is a layered shot composed of coffee liqueur (Kahlúa), Irish cream, and Grand Marnier. When prepared properly, the ingredients separate into three distinctly visible layers.

Bee’s Knees.title: Bee's knees
Bee’s Knees.desc: Prohibition Era cocktail made with gin
Bee’s Knees.text: A bees knees is a Prohibition era cocktail made with gin, fresh lemon juice, and honey. It is served shaken and chilled, often with a lemon twist.

Bellini.title: Bellini (cocktail)
Bellini.desc: Cocktail of Prosecco sparkling wine and peach purée
Bellini.text: A Bellini is a cocktail made with Prosecco and peach purée or nectar. It originated in Venice, Italy.

Between the Sheets.title: Between the sheets (cocktail)
Between the Sheets.text: The between the sheets is a cocktail consisting of white rum, cognac, triple sec, and lemon juice. When made with gin, instead of rum and cognac, it's called a "maiden's prayer".

Between the Sheets (Classic).title: Between the sheets (cocktail)
Between the Sheets (Classic).text: The between the sheets is a cocktail consisting of white rum, cognac, triple sec, and lemon juice. When made with gin, instead of rum and cognac, it's called a "maiden's prayer".

Between the Sheets (Our Ideal Recipe).title: Between the sheets (cocktail)
Between the Sheets (Our Ideal Recipe).text: The between the sheets is a cocktail consisting of white rum, cognac, triple sec, and lemon juice. When made with gin, instead of rum and cognac, it's called a "maiden's prayer".

Bijou.title: Bijou (cocktail)
Bijou.text: A bijou is a mixed alcoholic drink composed of gin, vermouth, and Chartreuse. This cocktail was invented by Harry Johnson, "the father of professional bartending", who called it bijou because it combined the colors of three jewels: gin for diamond, vermouth for ruby, and Chartreuse for emerald.

Black Russian.title: Black Russian
Black Russian.desc: Cocktail of vodka and coffee liqueur
Black Russian.text: The Black Russian is a cocktail of vodka and coffee liqueur. It contains 50 ml vodka and 20 ml coffee liqueur, per IBA specified ingredients.

Blackthorn.title: Blackthorn (cocktail)
Blackthorn.text: The Blackthorn is an Irish whiskey or sloe gin based cocktail. Both versions emerged in the late 19th and early 20th century.

Bloody Mary.title: Bloody Mary (cocktail)
Bloody Mary.desc: Cocktail of vodka and tomato juice
Bloody Mary.text: A Bloody Mary is a cocktail containing vodka, tomato juice, and other spices and flavorings including Worcestershire sauce, hot sauces, garlic, herbs, horseradish, celery, olives, pickled vegetables, salt, black pepper, lemon juice, lime juice and celery salt.

Bloody Mary (Classic Variation).title: Bloody Mary (cocktail)
Bloody Mary (Classic Variation).desc: Cocktail of vodka and tomato juice
Bloody Mary (Classic Variation).text: A Bloody Mary is a cocktail containing vodka, tomato juice, and other spices and flavorings including Worcestershire sauce, hot sauces, garlic, herbs, horseradish, celery, olives, pickled vegetables, salt, black pepper, lemon juice, lime juice and celery salt.

Boomerang.title: Boomerang (cocktail)
Boomerang.text: A Boomerang cocktail is a specific cocktail dating back to the early 20th century. In the 21st century, it may also be a reference to cocktails that bartenders illegally shuttle back and forth between bars as a way of sharing experimentation or building comradery.

Boston Sour.title: Whiskey sour
Boston Sour.text: A Whiskey Sour is a mixed drink or shot containing whiskey, lemon juice, and simple syrup, and traditionally garnished with a cherry or sometimes a lemon wedge. It is a blend of sour, bitter, and sweet flavors.

Boulevardier.title: Boulevardier (cocktail)
Boulevardier.desc: 1920s cocktail of whiskey, sweet vermouth, and Campari
Boulevardier.text: The boulevardier cocktail is an alcoholic drink composed of whiskey, sweet vermouth, and Campari. It originated as an obscure cocktail in late 1920s Paris, and was largely forgotten for 80 years, before being rediscovered in the late 2000s as part of the craft cocktail movement.

Bramble.title: Bramble (cocktail)
Bramble.text: The Bramble is a cocktail created by the British barman Dick Bradsell in 1980s London, England. Best described as a spring cocktail, the Bramble brings together dry gin, lemon juice, sugar syrup, crème de mûre, and crushed ice.

Brandy Alexander.title: Brandy Alexander
Brandy Alexander.desc: Brandy-based cocktail of cognac and crème de cacao
Brandy Alexander.text: A Brandy Alexander is a brandy-based dessert cocktail, consisting of cognac, crème de cacao, and cream, that became popular during the early 20th century. It is a variation of an earlier, gin-based cocktail called simply an Alexander.

Brandy Crusta.title: Brandy crusta
Brandy Crusta.text: A brandy crusta is an IBA Official Cocktail made of brandy, Maraschino Luxardo, curaçao, fresh lemon juice, sugar syrup, and Angostura bitters.

Brandy Flip.title: Flip (cocktail)
Brandy Flip.text: A flip is a class of mixed drink. According to the Oxford English Dictionary, the term was first used in 1695 to describe a mixture of beer, rum, and sugar, heated with a red-hot iron.

Brooklyn.title: Brooklyn (cocktail)
Brooklyn.text: The Brooklyn is one of five cocktails named for the boroughs of New York City, along with the Bronx, the Manhattan, the Queens and the Staten Island Ferry. It resembles a Manhattan, but with dry vermouth, Picon, and Maraschino.

Brown Derby.title: Brown Derby (cocktail)
Brown Derby.text: The Brown Derby, originally called the "De Rigueur" in cocktail books, is a three-ingredient cocktail that was named after the Brown Derby hat-shaped Los Angeles diner. It consists of bourbon, grapefruit juice, and honey syrup.

Caipirinha.title: Caipirinha
Caipirinha.text: Caipirinha is a Brazilian cocktail made with cachaça, sugar, lime, and ice. Originating in the state of São Paulo, the drink is prepared by mixing the fruit and the sugar together, then adding the liquor.

Canchanchara.title: Canchanchara
Canchanchara.desc: IBA official cocktail made with Cuban aguardiente, honey, and fresh lime juice
Canchanchara.text: The Canchanchara is an IBA official cocktail made with Cuban aguardiente, honey, and fresh lime juice.

Casino.title: Casino (cocktail)
Casino.text: The Casino is an IBA official cocktail made with gin, maraschino liqueur, orange bitters and fresh lemon juice.

Champagne Cocktail.title: Champagne cocktail
Champagne Cocktail.desc: Cocktail of champagne and Angostura bitters
Champagne Cocktail.text: A champagne cocktail is an alcoholic cocktail made with sugar, Angostura bitters, champagne, brandy, and a maraschino cherry as a garnish. It is one of the IBA official cocktails.

Chartreuse Swizzle.title: Chartreuse swizzle
Chartreuse Swizzle.desc: Cocktail with Chartreuse, Falernum, pineapple juice, and lime juice
Chartreuse Swizzle.text: The Chartreuse swizzle is a tiki cocktail made with green Chartreuse, velvet falernum, pineapple juice, and lime juice. Invented in 2003 by American bartender Marcovaldo Dionysos of San Francisco cocktail bar Harry Denton's Starlight Room, the cocktail has since emerged as a modern classic.

Chrysanthemum.title: Chrysanthemum (cocktail)
Chrysanthemum.text: The Chrysanthemum is a cocktail made with absinthe, Bénédictine, and vermouth.

Clover Club.title: Clover Club cocktail
Clover Club.text: A Clover Club cocktail is a shaken cocktail consisting of gin, lemon juice, raspberry syrup, and egg white. The egg white acts as an emulsifier, forming the drink's characteristic foamy head.

Corpse Reviver.title: Corpse reviver
Corpse Reviver.desc: Family of cocktails intended for curing hangovers
Corpse Reviver.text: The corpse reviver family of named cocktails are sometimes drunk as alcoholic hangover tongue-in-cheek "cures", of potency or characteristics to be able to revive even a dead person.

Corpse Reviver #2.title: Corpse reviver
Corpse Reviver #2.desc: Family of cocktails intended for curing hangovers
Corpse Reviver #2.text: The corpse reviver family of named cocktails are sometimes drunk as alcoholic hangover tongue-in-cheek "cures", of potency or characteristics to be able to revive even a dead person.

Cosmopolitan.title: Cosmopolitan (cocktail)
Cosmopolitan.text: A cosmopolitan, or, informally, a cosmo, is a cocktail made with vodka, Cointreau, cranberry juice, and freshly squeezed or sweetened lime juice. The traditional garnish is a lime slice but a twist or wedge can be used instead.

Cuba Libra.title: Rum and Coke
Cuba Libra.text: Rum and Coke, or the Cuba libre, is a highball cocktail consisting of cola, rum, and in many recipes lime juice on ice.

Cuba Libre.title: Rum and Coke
Cuba Libre.text: Rum and Coke, or the Cuba libre, is a highball cocktail consisting of cola, rum, and in many recipes lime juice on ice.

Daiquiri.title: Daiquiri
Daiquiri.text: The daiquiri is a cocktail whose main ingredients are rum, citrus juice, and sugar or other sweetener.

Dark 'n' Stormy.title: Dark 'n' stormy
Dark 'n' Stormy.text: A dark 'n' stormy is a highball cocktail made with dark rum and ginger beer served over ice and garnished with a slice of lime. Lime juice and simple syrup are also frequently added.

Dark and Stormy.title: Dark 'n' stormy
Dark and Stormy.text: A dark 'n' stormy is a highball cocktail made with dark rum and ginger beer served over ice and garnished with a slice of lime. Lime juice and simple syrup are also frequently added.

Death in the Afternoon.title: Death in the Afternoon (cocktail)
Death in the Afternoon.desc: Cocktail made up of absinthe and Champagne
Death in the Afternoon.text: Death in the Afternoon, also called the Hemingway or the Hemingway Champagne, is a cocktail made up of absinthe and Champagne, invented by Ernest Hemingway.

Derby.title: Derby (cocktail)
Derby.text: The derby is a cocktail composed of gin, peach bitters and mint leaves.

photo.artist: Michael Styne from Averill Park, NY, USA

Dirty Martini.title: Martini (cocktail)
Dirty Martini.desc: Cocktail made with gin and vermouth
Dirty Martini.text: The martini is a cocktail made with gin and vermouth, garnished with an olive, a lemon twist, or both. Over the years, the martini has become one of the best-known mixed alcoholic beverages worldwide.

Dry Martini.title: Martini (cocktail)
Dry Martini.desc: Cocktail made with gin and vermouth
Dry Martini.text: The martini is a cocktail made with gin and vermouth, garnished with an olive, a lemon twist, or both. Over the years, the martini has become one of the best-known mixed alcoholic beverages worldwide.

Eggnog.title: Eggnog
Eggnog.text: Eggnog, historically also known as milk punch or egg milk punch, is a rich, chilled, sweetened, creamy dairy-based beverage traditionally made with milk or cream, sugar, whipped eggs and, in some contexts, distilled spirits such as brandy, rum or bourbon.

Fernandito.title: Fernet con coca
Fernandito.desc: Argentine cocktail made of fernet and cola
Fernandito.text: Fernet con coca, also known as fernando, its diminutive fernandito, or several other nicknames, is a long drink of Argentine origin consisting of the Italian amaro liqueur fernet and cola, served over ice.

Fish House Punch.title: Fish house punch
Fish House Punch.text: Fish house punch is a strong, rum-based punch containing rum, cognac, and peach brandy. The drink is typically served over an ice block in a punch bowl and garnished with lemon slices.

Flaming Dr. Pepper.title: Flaming Doctor Pepper
Flaming Dr. Pepper.text: A Flaming Doctor Pepper, or Flaming Dr Pepper, is a flaming cocktail with taste similar to the soft drink Dr Pepper, despite Dr Pepper not being one of its ingredients. Dave Brinks of the Gold Mine Saloon lays claim to inventing the drink.

Flip.title: Flip (cocktail)
Flip.text: A flip is a class of mixed drink. According to the Oxford English Dictionary, the term was first used in 1695 to describe a mixture of beer, rum, and sugar, heated with a red-hot iron.

French 75.title: French 75 (cocktail)
French 75.desc: Cocktail made from gin (or cognac), Champagne, lemon juice, and sugar
French 75.text: French 75 is a cocktail made from gin, champagne, lemon juice, and sugar. It is also called a 75 cocktail, or in French simply a soixante quinze.

Frozen Daiquiri.title: Daiquiri
Frozen Daiquiri.text: The daiquiri is a cocktail whose main ingredients are rum, citrus juice, and sugar or other sweetener.

Frozen Mint Daiquiri.title: Daiquiri
Frozen Mint Daiquiri.text: The daiquiri is a cocktail whose main ingredients are rum, citrus juice, and sugar or other sweetener.

Frozen Pineapple Daiquiri.title: Daiquiri
Frozen Pineapple Daiquiri.text: The daiquiri is a cocktail whose main ingredients are rum, citrus juice, and sugar or other sweetener.

Garibaldi.title: Garibaldi (cocktail)
Garibaldi.desc: Cocktail of Campari and orange juice
Garibaldi.text: The Garibaldi is an Italian aperitivo cocktail made with Campari and freshly squeezed orange juice, typically served over ice. The drink is named after Giuseppe Garibaldi, the 19th-century Italian general associated with the movement toward Italian unification.

Gibson.title: Gibson (cocktail)
Gibson.desc: Gin and vermouth cocktail, often served with an onion
Gibson.text: The Gibson is a mixed drink made with gin and dry vermouth, and often garnished with a pickled onion. In its modern incarnation, it is considered a cousin of the martini, distinguished mostly by garnishing with an onion instead of an olive.

Gimlet.title: Gimlet (cocktail)
Gimlet.text: The gimlet is a cocktail made of gin and lime cordial. A 1928 description of the drink was: gin, and a spot of lime.

Gin and Tonic.title: Gin and tonic
Gin and Tonic.desc: Drink made with gin and tonic water
Gin and Tonic.text: A gin and tonic is a highball cocktail made with gin and tonic water poured over ice. The ratio of gin to tonic varies according to taste, strength of the gin, other drink mixers being added, etc., with most recipes calling for a ratio between 1:1 and 1:3.

Gin Basil Smash.title: Gin basil smash
Gin Basil Smash.desc: Cocktail of gin, lemon, sugar, and basil
Gin Basil Smash.text: The gin basil smash is a cocktail consisting of gin, lemon juice, simple syrup, and Genovese basil. It is a type of smash, a cocktail made of muddled fruit or herbs.

Gin Fizz.title: Fizz (cocktail)
Gin Fizz.desc: Type of carbonated alcoholic mixed drinks
Gin Fizz.text: A "fizz" is a mixed drink variation on the older sours family of cocktail. Its defining features are an acidic juice and carbonated water.

Gin Rickey.title: Rickey (cocktail)
Gin Rickey.desc: Highball drink made from gin or bourbon
Gin Rickey.text: The rickey is a highball made from gin or bourbon, lime juice, and carbonated water. Little or no sugar is added to the rickey.

Gin Sour.title: Sour (cocktail)
Gin Sour.text: A sour is a traditional family of mixed drinks. Sours belong to one of the old families of original cocktails and are described by Jerry Thomas in his 1862 book How to Mix Drinks.

Gin Tonic.title: Gin and tonic
Gin Tonic.desc: Drink made with gin and tonic water
Gin Tonic.text: A gin and tonic is a highball cocktail made with gin and tonic water poured over ice. The ratio of gin to tonic varies according to taste, strength of the gin, other drink mixers being added, etc., with most recipes calling for a ratio between 1:1 and 1:3.

Godfather.title: Godfather (cocktail)
Godfather.desc: Cocktail made of scotch and amaretto
Godfather.text: The Godfather is a duo mixed drink made of Scotch whisky and amaretto. Typically, the drink is served with ice in an old fashioned glass.

Grasshopper.title: Grasshopper (cocktail)
Grasshopper.text: A grasshopper is a sweet, mint-flavored, after-dinner alcoholic drink named for its green color, which comes from crème de menthe. Tujague's, a bar in the French Quarter of New Orleans, Louisiana, claims its owner Philip Guichet invented the drink in 1918.

Greyhound.title: Greyhound (cocktail)
Greyhound.desc: Cocktail made with grapefruit juice and gin or vodka
Greyhound.text: A greyhound is a cocktail consisting of grapefruit juice and gin or vodka mixed and served over ice. If the rim of the glass has been salted, the drink is instead called a salty dog.

Hanky Panky.title: Hanky panky (cocktail)
Hanky Panky.text: The hanky panky is a cocktail made from gin, sweet vermouth, and Fernet-Branca. It is a variation on the sweet martini, or Martinez, made distinctive by the Fernet-Branca, a bitter Italian digestivo.

Harvey Wallbanger.title: Harvey Wallbanger
Harvey Wallbanger.text: The Harvey Wallbanger is a mixed drink made with vodka, Galliano, and orange juice. It is a variant of the screwdriver, and was very popular in the United States in the 1970s.

Hemingway Daiquiri.title: Hemingway special
Hemingway Daiquiri.text: A Hemingway special is an all day cocktail based on the Floridita daiquiri. It is recognised as an IBA official cocktail by the IBA.

Hemingway Special.title: Hemingway special
Hemingway Special.text: A Hemingway special is an all day cocktail based on the Floridita daiquiri. It is recognised as an IBA official cocktail by the IBA.

Horse's Neck.title: Horse's neck
Horse's Neck.desc: Cocktail made with brandy and ginger ale
Horse's Neck.text: A horse's neck is a cocktail recognised by the International Bartenders Association (IBA), identifiably sporting a long, curling strip of lemon rind.

Hot Toddy.title: Hot toddy
Hot Toddy.text: A hot toddy, also known as hot whiskey in Ireland, and occasionally called southern cough syrup within the Southern United States, is typically a mixed drink made of liquor and water with honey, lemon, and spices, and served hot.

Hurricane.title: Hurricane (cocktail)
Hurricane.text: The Hurricane cocktail is a sweet alcoholic drink made with rum, lemon juice, and either passion fruit syrup or fassionola. It is one of many popular drinks served in New Orleans.

Illegal.title: Illegal (cocktail)
Illegal.text: The Illegal is an IBA official cocktail. This cocktail is named after the mezcal brand Ilegal Mezcal, which is one of its key ingredients.

Irish Coffee.title: Irish coffee
Irish Coffee.desc: Drink containing coffee, whiskey and whipped cream
Irish Coffee.text: Irish coffee is a caffeinated alcoholic drink consisting of Irish whiskey, hot coffee and sugar, which has been stirred and topped with cream. The coffee is drunk through the cream.

Jack Rose Cocktail.title: Jack Rose (cocktail)
Jack Rose Cocktail.desc: Cocktail of applejack, grenadine and citrus juice popular in the 1920s and 1930s
Jack Rose Cocktail.text: A Jack Rose is a cocktail containing applejack, grenadine, and lemon or lime juice.

John Collins.title: John Collins (cocktail)
John Collins.desc: Long drink of London dry gin, lemon juice, sugar and carbonated water
John Collins.text: A John Collins is a long drink of London dry gin, lemon juice, sugar and carbonated water, which was attested in 1869, but may be older.

photo.artist: Michael Styne from Averill Park, NY, USA

Jungle Bird.title: Jungle Bird
Jungle Bird.desc: Cocktail with blackstrap rum, Campari, pineapple juice, lime juice, and demerara syrup
Jungle Bird.text: The Jungle Bird is a tiki cocktail made with blackstrap rum, Campari, pineapple juice, lime juice, and demerara syrup. Invented by Malaysian beverage manager Jeffrey Ong in 1973, it has been recognized by the International Bartenders Association as an official cocktail since 2024.

Kamikaze.title: Kamikaze (cocktail)
Kamikaze.desc: Cocktail of vodka, triple sec and lime juice
Kamikaze.text: The Kamikaze is a cocktail made of equal parts vodka, triple sec and lime juice. Garnish is typically a wedge or twist of lime.

Kir.title: Kir (cocktail)
Kir.desc: French cocktail with crème de cassis and white wine
Kir.text: Kir is a French cocktail made with a measure of crème de cassis topped up with white wine.

Kir Royale.title: Kir royal
Kir Royale.text: The Kir royal, also known as Kir royale, is a French cocktail, a variation on the Kir. It consists of crème de cassis topped with champagne, rather than the white wine used in traditional Kir.

Last Word.title: Last Word (cocktail)
Last Word.text: The Last Word is a gin-based cocktail originating at the Detroit Athletic Club in the 1910s, shortly before the start of Prohibition.

Lemon Drop.title: Lemon drop (cocktail)
Lemon Drop.text: A lemon drop is a vodka-based cocktail that has a lemony, sweet and sour flavor, prepared using vodka, triple sec, and fresh lemon juice. It has been described as a variant of, or as "a take on", the vodka martini, but is in fact closer to a daisy or a white lady variant.

photo.artist: Schezar from New York City, USA

Long Island Tea.title: Long Island iced tea
Long Island Tea.desc: Mixed drink with vodka, gin, tequila, and rum
Long Island Tea.text: The Long Island iced tea, or Long Island ice tea, is an IBA official cocktail, typically made with vodka, tequila, white rum, Cointreau, gin, and a splash of cola. Despite its name, the cocktail does not typically contain iced tea, but is named due to having a similar amber hue as iced tea.

photo.artist: Eduardo Quagliato from Curitiba, Paraná, Brasil

Long vodka.title: Long vodka
Long vodka.text: A long vodka is a vodka-based cocktail, popular throughout Scotland and known to be served in some parts of England.

Mai Tai.title: Mai Tai
Mai Tai.desc: Cocktail based on rum, Curaçao liqueur and lime juice
Mai Tai.text: The Mai Tai is a cocktail made of rum, Curaçao liqueur, orgeat syrup, and lime juice. It is one of the characteristic cocktails in Tiki culture.

Manhattan.title: Manhattan (cocktail)
Manhattan.desc: Cocktail made with whiskey, sweet vermouth, and bitters
Manhattan.text: A Manhattan is a cocktail made with whiskey, sweet vermouth, and bitters. While rye is the traditional whiskey of choice, other commonly used whiskies include Canadian whisky, bourbon, blended whiskey, and Tennessee whiskey.

Margarita.title: Margarita
Margarita.desc: Mexican cocktail of tequila, triple sec, and lime juice
Margarita.text: A margarita is a cocktail made of tequila, triple sec, lime juice, and sometimes simple syrup. It is served shaken with ice, without ice, or blended with ice (frozen).

Margarita (Dry).title: Margarita
Margarita (Dry).desc: Mexican cocktail of tequila, triple sec, and lime juice
Margarita (Dry).text: A margarita is a cocktail made of tequila, triple sec, lime juice, and sometimes simple syrup. It is served shaken with ice, without ice, or blended with ice (frozen).

Margarita (Sweet).title: Margarita
Margarita (Sweet).desc: Mexican cocktail of tequila, triple sec, and lime juice
Margarita (Sweet).text: A margarita is a cocktail made of tequila, triple sec, lime juice, and sometimes simple syrup. It is served shaken with ice, without ice, or blended with ice (frozen).

Martinez.title: Martinez (cocktail)
Martinez.desc: Cocktail made with Old Tom gin and vermouth
Martinez.text: The Martinez is a classic cocktail that is widely regarded as the direct precursor to the Martini. It serves as the basis for many modern cocktails, and several different versions of the original exist.

Martini.title: Martini (cocktail)
Martini.desc: Cocktail made with gin and vermouth
Martini.text: The martini is a cocktail made with gin and vermouth, garnished with an olive, a lemon twist, or both. Over the years, the martini has become one of the best-known mixed alcoholic beverages worldwide.

Martini (Our Root Recipe).title: Martini (cocktail)
Martini (Our Root Recipe).desc: Cocktail made with gin and vermouth
Martini (Our Root Recipe).text: The martini is a cocktail made with gin and vermouth, garnished with an olive, a lemon twist, or both. Over the years, the martini has become one of the best-known mixed alcoholic beverages worldwide.

Martini (Very Dry).title: Martini (cocktail)
Martini (Very Dry).desc: Cocktail made with gin and vermouth
Martini (Very Dry).text: The martini is a cocktail made with gin and vermouth, garnished with an olive, a lemon twist, or both. Over the years, the martini has become one of the best-known mixed alcoholic beverages worldwide.

Martini (Wet).title: Martini (cocktail)
Martini (Wet).desc: Cocktail made with gin and vermouth
Martini (Wet).text: The martini is a cocktail made with gin and vermouth, garnished with an olive, a lemon twist, or both. Over the years, the martini has become one of the best-known mixed alcoholic beverages worldwide.

Mary Pickford.title: Mary Pickford (cocktail)
Mary Pickford.text: A Mary Pickford is a Prohibition era cocktail made with white rum, fresh pineapple juice, grenadine, and maraschino liqueur. It is served shaken and chilled, often with a maraschino cherry.

Michelada.title: Michelada
Michelada.desc: Mexican drink made with beer, lime juice, assorted sauces, and spices
Michelada.text: A michelada is a Mexican drink made with beer, lime juice, assorted sauces, spices, and chili peppers. It is served in a chilled, salt-rimmed glass.

Mimosa.title: Mimosa (cocktail)
Mimosa.text: A mimosa cocktail consists of champagne and chilled citrus juice, usually orange juice. It is often served in a tall champagne flute at brunch, or at festive occasions such as weddings, or as part of business or first class service on some passenger railways and airlines.

Mint Julep.title: Mint julep
Mint Julep.desc: Cocktail of bourbon, sugar and fresh mint
Mint Julep.text: Mint julep is an alcoholic cocktail, consisting primarily of bourbon, sugar, water, crushed or shaved ice, and fresh mint. As a bourbon-based cocktail, it is associated with the American South and the cuisine of the Southern United States in general, in particular as a symbol of the Kentucky Derby.

Mojito.title: Mojito
Mojito.text: Mojito is a traditional Cuban punch. The cocktail often consists of five ingredients: white rum, sugar, lime juice, soda water, and mint.

Monkey Gland.title: Monkey gland (cocktail)
Monkey Gland.text: The Monkey Gland is a cocktail of gin, orange juice, grenadine and absinthe created in the 1920s by Harry MacElhone, owner of the famous Harry's New York Bar in Paris, France.

Moscow Mule.title: Moscow mule
Moscow Mule.text: A Moscow mule is a cocktail made with vodka, ginger beer, and lime juice; garnished with a slice or wedge of lime. The drink, being a type of buck, is sometimes called vodka buck.

Mulled Wine.title: Mulled wine
Mulled Wine.text: Mulled wine, also known as spiced wine, is an alcoholic drink usually made with red wine, along with various mulling spices and sometimes raisins, served hot or warm. It is a traditional drink during winter, especially around Christmas.

Naked and Famous.title: Naked and famous (cocktail)
Naked and Famous.text: The naked and famous is an IBA official cocktail, consisting of equal parts mezcal, yellow Chartreuse, Aperol, and fresh lime juice.

Negroni.title: Negroni
Negroni.desc: Cocktail made of gin, vermouth, and Campari
Negroni.text: A Negroni is an Italian cocktail, made of equal parts gin, vermouth rosso, and Campari, generally served with ice, and commonly garnished with an orange slice or orange peel. It is considered an apéritif.

New York Sour.title: New York sour
New York Sour.text: The New York sour is an IBA official cocktail. Largely similar to the whiskey sour, the New York sour adds a float of dry red wine to the drink.

Old Cuban.title: Old Cuban
Old Cuban.text: The Old Cuban was created in 2001 by mixologist Audrey Saunders. It is also an IBA official cocktail.

Old Fashioned.title: Old fashioned (cocktail)
Old Fashioned.desc: Cocktail made with whiskey, bitters and sugar
Old Fashioned.text: The old fashioned is a cocktail made by muddling sugar with bitters and water, adding whiskey or sometimes brandy, and garnishing with an orange slice or zest and a cocktail cherry. It is traditionally served with ice in an old fashioned glass.

Old Pal.title: Old pal
Old Pal.desc: Cocktail of whiskey, vermouth and Campari
Old Pal.text: The old pal is a cocktail consisting of equal parts rye whiskey, French vermouth (dry), and Campari.

Old-Fashioned.title: Old fashioned (cocktail)
Old-Fashioned.desc: Cocktail made with whiskey, bitters and sugar
Old-Fashioned.text: The old fashioned is a cocktail made by muddling sugar with bitters and water, adding whiskey or sometimes brandy, and garnishing with an orange slice or zest and a cocktail cherry. It is traditionally served with ice in an old fashioned glass.

Orange Whip.title: Orange whip
Orange Whip.text: An orange whip is a sweet cocktail made with rum, vodka, cream and orange juice. It is typically blended to a froth like a milkshake, and poured over ice in a Collins glass.

Orgasm.title: Orgasm (cocktail)
Orgasm.text: The orgasm is a cocktail that can be served either on the rocks or layered and drunk as a shooter.

Paloma.title: Paloma (cocktail)
Paloma.text: The paloma is a tequila-based cocktail. This drink is most commonly prepared by mixing tequila, lime juice, and a grapefruit-flavored soda such as Fresca, Squirt, or Jarritos and served with ice and a lime wedge.

Paper Plane.title: Paper plane (cocktail)
Paper Plane.text: The paper plane is a whiskey-based cocktail created in 2008. In 2020 it was added to the International Bartenders Association's (IBA) list of official cocktails as a new era drink.

Paradise.title: Paradise (cocktail)
Paradise.desc: Apéritif of gin, apricot brandy and orange juice
Paradise.text: The Paradise is an IBA official cocktail, and is classified as a "pre-dinner" drink, an apéritif.

Pegu Club.title: Pegu Club (cocktail)
Pegu Club.text: The Pegu Club or the Pegu is a gin-based cocktail that was the signature drink of Burma's Pegu Club. Located just outside Rangoon, the club was named after the Pegu, a Burmese river, and its members were those Britons who were senior government and military officials and prominent businessmen.

Penicillin.title: Penicillin (cocktail)
Penicillin.text: The Penicillin is an IBA official cocktail made with Scotch whisky, ginger, honey syrup, and fresh lemon juice.

Perfect Manhattan.title: Manhattan (cocktail)
Perfect Manhattan.desc: Cocktail made with whiskey, sweet vermouth, and bitters
Perfect Manhattan.text: A Manhattan is a cocktail made with whiskey, sweet vermouth, and bitters. While rye is the traditional whiskey of choice, other commonly used whiskies include Canadian whisky, bourbon, blended whiskey, and Tennessee whiskey.

Pimm's Cup.title: Pimm's cup
Pimm's Cup.text: The Pimm's cup is a cocktail that is popular in England, in the United Kingdom. It is one of numerous fruit cups, a type of cocktail with gin, a soft drink, and fruit.

Pina Colada.title: Piña colada
Pina Colada.desc: Puerto Rican cocktail with rum, coconut, and pineapple
Pina Colada.text: The piña colada is a cocktail made with rum, cream of coconut and pineapple juice, usually served either shaken with ice or blended. It it usually garnished with either a pineapple wedge or a maraschino cherry, or both.

Pink Gin.title: Pink gin
Pink Gin.desc: Cocktail of gin and bitters; also a fruit-flavoured style of gin
Pink Gin.text: Pink gin is a traditional cocktail fashionable in England from the mid-19th century, consisting of Plymouth gin and a dash of Angostura bitters, colouring the drink pink. The cocktail is typically topped up with water.

Pink Lady.title: Pink lady (cocktail)
Pink Lady.text: The pink lady is a classic gin-based cocktail with a long history. Its pink color comes from grenadine.

Pisco Punch.title: Pisco punch
Pisco Punch.text: Pisco punch is an alcoholic beverage made famous by Duncan Nicol at the Bank Exchange Saloon at the end of the 19th century, in San Francisco, California.

Pisco Sour.title: Pisco sour
Pisco Sour.desc: Cocktail in Chilean and Peruvian cuisine
Pisco Sour.text: A pisco sour is an alcoholic cocktail of Peruvian origin, which is made from pisco, a Peruvian brandy, with sour citrus juice and sweetener components. The Peruvian pisco sour includes Peruvian pisco with freshly squeezed lime juice, simple syrup, ice, egg white, and Angostura bitters.

Planter's Punch.title: Planter's punch
Planter's Punch.text: Planter's punch is an IBA Official Cocktail made of Jamaican rum, fresh lime juice, and sugar cane juice. The cocktail originated in Jamaica.

Porto flip.title: Porto flip
Porto flip.text: A Porto flip is a type of drink. It is typically made with brandy, ruby port, and one egg yolk.

Rabo de Galo.title: Rabo de Galo
Rabo de Galo.text: Rabo de Galo is a Brazilian cocktail made with cachaça, sweet vermouth and Cynar, and is one of the official cocktails recognised by the International Bartenders Association (IBA), which lists it among the Contemporary Classics.

Ramos Gin Fizz.title: Fizz (cocktail)
Ramos Gin Fizz.desc: Type of carbonated alcoholic mixed drinks
Ramos Gin Fizz.text: A "fizz" is a mixed drink variation on the older sours family of cocktail. Its defining features are an acidic juice and carbonated water.

Remember the Maine.title: Remember the Maine (cocktail)
Remember the Maine.text: The Remember the Maine is an IBA official cocktail made with rye whiskey, cherry brandy, sweet vermouth, and absinthe. The Gentleman’s Companion, by Charles H. Baker, Jr. states that he encountered the cocktail in Havana, Cuba during the Cuban Revolution of 1933.

Rob Roy.title: Rob Roy (cocktail)
Rob Roy.text: The Rob Roy is a cocktail consisting primarily of Scotch whisky and vermouth, created in 1894 by a bartender at the Waldorf Astoria in Manhattan, New York City.

Rose.title: Rose (cocktail)
Rose.desc: Cocktail of vermouth, Kirsch and fruit syrup
Rose.text: Rose is a cocktail made of vermouth, Kirschwasser and fruit syrup. Some recipes include cherry liqueur and gin.

Rum Punch.title: Punch (drink)
Rum Punch.desc: Drink containing fruit or fruit juice
Rum Punch.text: The term punch refers to a wide assortment of drinks, both alcoholic and non-alcoholic, generally containing fruits or fruit juice. The drink was introduced from the Indian subcontinent to England by employees of the East India Company in the late 17th century.

Rum Sour.title: Sour (cocktail)
Rum Sour.text: A sour is a traditional family of mixed drinks. Sours belong to one of the old families of original cocktails and are described by Jerry Thomas in his 1862 book How to Mix Drinks.

Rusty Nail.title: Rusty nail (cocktail)
Rusty Nail.desc: Cocktail mixing Drambuie and Scotch whisky
Rusty Nail.text: A rusty nail is a cocktail made by mixing Scotch whisky with Drambuie in a ratio ranging from 1:1 to 2:1. It is typically served on the rocks in an old-fashioned glass, though it can be served "up" in a stemmed glass.

Salty Dog.title: Salty dog (cocktail)
Salty Dog.desc: Cocktail of gin or vodka and grapefruit juice
Salty Dog.text: A salty dog is a cocktail made with gin or vodka and grapefruit juice, served in a highball glass with a salted rim. The salt distinguishes it from the related greyhound.

Sazerac.title: Sazerac
Sazerac.text: Sazerac is a local variation of a cognac or whiskey cocktail originally from New Orleans. It is named for the Sazerac de Forge et Fils brand of cognac brandy that originally served as its main ingredient.

Scotch Sour.title: Whiskey sour
Scotch Sour.text: A Whiskey Sour is a mixed drink or shot containing whiskey, lemon juice, and simple syrup, and traditionally garnished with a cherry or sometimes a lemon wedge. It is a blend of sour, bitter, and sweet flavors.

Screwdriver.title: Screwdriver (cocktail)
Screwdriver.desc: Highball drink made with fresh orange juice and vodka
Screwdriver.text: A screwdriver is an alcoholic highball drink made with orange juice and vodka. In the UK, it is referred to as a "vodka and orange".

Sea breeze.title: Sea breeze (cocktail)
Sea breeze.desc: Cocktail of vodka with cranberry and grapefruit juice
Sea breeze.text: A sea breeze is a cocktail containing vodka with cranberry juice and grapefruit juice. The cocktail is usually consumed during summer months.

Sherry Cobbler.title: Sherry cobbler
Sherry Cobbler.text: A sherry cobbler is a classic American cocktail made with sherry, sugar and citrus. Its origins are not known in detail, but is believed to have originated sometime in the early 19th century.

Sherry Flip.title: Flip (cocktail)
Sherry Flip.text: A flip is a class of mixed drink. According to the Oxford English Dictionary, the term was first used in 1695 to describe a mixture of beer, rum, and sugar, heated with a red-hot iron.

Sidecar.title: Sidecar (cocktail)
Sidecar.desc: Cocktail made with cognac, orange liqueur, and lemon
Sidecar.text: The sidecar is a cocktail traditionally made with brandy, orange liqueur, and lemon juice. It became popular in Paris and London in the early 1920s.

Sidecar (Our Ideal Recipe).title: Sidecar (cocktail)
Sidecar (Our Ideal Recipe).desc: Cocktail made with cognac, orange liqueur, and lemon
Sidecar (Our Ideal Recipe).text: The sidecar is a cocktail traditionally made with brandy, orange liqueur, and lemon juice. It became popular in Paris and London in the early 1920s.

Singapore Sling.title: Singapore sling
Singapore Sling.desc: Cocktail with gin and cherry liqueur
Singapore Sling.text: The Singapore sling is a gin-based sling cocktail from Singapore. This long drink was reputed to have been developed in 1915 by Ngiam Tong Boon, a bartender at the Long Bar in Raffles Hotel, Singapore.

Sol Y Sombra.title: Sol y Sombra
Sol Y Sombra.text: Sol y sombra is an after dinner or breakfast alcoholic drink, consisting of equal parts brandy and anise dulce served in a brandy snifter, that is well known in Madrid and Spain generally. This is more than a single shot and is poured in a ratio of five seconds per each component.

South Side.title: South Side (cocktail)
South Side.text: A South Side or Southside is an alcoholic beverage made with gin, lemon juice, simple syrup and mint. A variant, the Southside Fizz, adds soda water.

Southside.title: South Side (cocktail)
