Southside.text: A South Side or Southside is an alcoholic beverage made with gin, lemon juice, simple syrup and mint. A variant, the Southside Fizz, adds soda water.

Spicy Fifty.title: Spicy Fifty
Spicy Fifty.text: A Spicy Fifty is a cocktail containing vanilla-flavored vodka with elderflower cordial, lime juice, honey syrup, and red chili pepper. To prepare, the ingredients are added to a cocktail shaker and shaken with ice.

Spritz.title: Spritz (cocktail)
Spritz.text: A spritz is an Italian wine-based cocktail, commonly served as an apéritif across Italy. It consists of Prosecco, a mixer, and a flavouring ingredient, which can be a bitter liqueur, a bitter apéritif, an amaro or a syrup.

Stinger.title: Stinger (cocktail)
Stinger.desc: Cocktail made from crème de menthe and brandy
Stinger.text: A stinger is a duo cocktail made by adding crème de menthe to brandy. The cocktail's origins can be traced to the United States in the 1890s, and the beverage remained widely popular in America until the 1970s.

Suffering Bastard.title: Suffering bastard
Suffering Bastard.text: The suffering bastard is the name for two different mixed drinks, one being more of a standard cocktail associated with World War II and the other being more of an exotic drink associated with Tiki bars.

Tequila Sour.title: Sour (cocktail)
Tequila Sour.text: A sour is a traditional family of mixed drinks. Sours belong to one of the old families of original cocktails and are described by Jerry Thomas in his 1862 book How to Mix Drinks.

Tequila Sunrise.title: Tequila sunrise
Tequila Sunrise.text: The tequila sunrise is a cocktail made of tequila, orange juice, and grenadine syrup. The drink is served unmixed in a tall glass.

The Last Word.title: Last Word (cocktail)
The Last Word.text: The Last Word is a gin-based cocktail originating at the Detroit Athletic Club in the 1910s, shortly before the start of Prohibition.

Ti’ Punch.title: Ti' punch
Ti’ Punch.text: Ti' punch literally meaning "small punch", is a rum-based mixed drink that is especially popular in Martinique, Guadeloupe, Saint Martin, Haiti, French Guiana, Réunion, Saint Lucia, and other French-speaking Caribbean islands. It is also the national cocktail of Martinique and Guadeloupe.

Tom and Jerry.title: Tom and Jerry (drink)
Tom and Jerry.desc: Christmas-time cocktail in the United States
Tom and Jerry.text: A Tom and Jerry is a traditional Christmas-time cocktail in the United States, sometimes attributed to British writer and boxing journalist Pierce Egan in the 1820s. It is a variant of eggnog with brandy and rum added and served hot, usually in a mug or a bowl.

Tom Collins.title: Tom Collins
Tom Collins.desc: Cocktail made from gin, lemon juice, sugar and club soda
Tom Collins.text: The Tom Collins is a Collins cocktail made from gin, lemon juice, sugar, and carbonated water. This "gin and sparkling lemonade" drink is typically served in a Collins glass over ice with a cherry garnish.

Tommy's Margarita.title: Tommy's margarita
Tommy's Margarita.text: Tommy's margarita is a variant of the margarita cocktail that uses agave nectar instead of triple sec and simple syrup. It is recognized by the IBA as a new era drink.

Trinidad Sour.title: Trinidad sour
Trinidad Sour.text: The Trinidad Sour is an IBA official cocktail. Unusually for a cocktail, it uses Angostura bitters as its base spirit rather than merely as a flavoring agent.

Tuxedo.title: Tuxedo (cocktail)
Tuxedo.text: The tuxedo is an IBA Official Cocktail composed of gin, dry vermouth, orange bitters, maraschino and absinthe.

Tuxedo Cocktail.title: Tuxedo (cocktail)
Tuxedo Cocktail.text: The tuxedo is an IBA Official Cocktail composed of gin, dry vermouth, orange bitters, maraschino and absinthe.

Vampiro.title: Vampiro (cocktail)
Vampiro.text: The vampiro is a cocktail that includes fruit juice, spices, fruit soda, fresh lime juice, and tequila. The vampiro has a fruity, lightly carbonated, and spicy taste.

Ve.n.to.title: Ve.n.to
Ve.n.to.text: The Ve.n.to, sometimes referred to as the Vento, is a cocktail made of grappa, fresh lemon juice, honey, and chamomile cordial, with an optional egg white.

Vesper.title: Vesper (cocktail)
Vesper.desc: Cocktail originally made of gin, vodka and Kina Lillet
Vesper.text: The Vesper is a cocktail that was originally made of gin, vodka, and Kina Lillet. Since that form of Lillet is no longer produced, modern bartenders need to modify the recipe to mimic the original taste, with Lillet Blanc or Cocchi Americano as a typical substitute.

Vieux Carré.title: Vieux Carré (cocktail)
Vieux Carré.desc: Cocktail made with whiskey, brandy, and Bénédictine
Vieux Carré.text: The Vieux Carré is an IBA official cocktail made with rye whiskey, cognac, sweet vermouth, Bénédictine, and Peychaud's bitters. It originated with Walter Bergeron, a bartender at the Carousel Bar in Hotel Monteleone, New Orleans.

Vodka And Tonic.title: Vodka tonic
Vodka And Tonic.text: A vodka tonic is a long drink made with varying proportions of vodka and tonic water. Vodka tonics are frequently garnished with a slice of lime or lemon.

Vodka Martini.title: Martini (cocktail)
Vodka Martini.desc: Cocktail made with gin and vermouth
Vodka Martini.text: The martini is a cocktail made with gin and vermouth, garnished with an olive, a lemon twist, or both. Over the years, the martini has become one of the best-known mixed alcoholic beverages worldwide.

Vodka Tonic.title: Vodka tonic
Vodka Tonic.text: A vodka tonic is a long drink made with varying proportions of vodka and tonic water. Vodka tonics are frequently garnished with a slice of lime or lemon.

Whiskey Sour.title: Whiskey sour
Whiskey Sour.text: A Whiskey Sour is a mixed drink or shot containing whiskey, lemon juice, and simple syrup, and traditionally garnished with a cherry or sometimes a lemon wedge. It is a blend of sour, bitter, and sweet flavors.

Whisky Highball.title: Highball
Whisky Highball.text: The highball is defined as an alcoholic beverage that is "built in a highball glass" and which calls "for a base spirit and mixer, such as soda or water." It is a type of long drink consisting of one or two parts of liquor, mixed over ice with upwards of two parts of a typically carbonated mixer.

Whisky Mac.title: Whisky Mac
Whisky Mac.desc: Cocktail with whisky and ginger wine
Whisky Mac.text: A Whisky Macdonald, more commonly known under the shortened name Whisky Mac, is a cocktail made up of whisky and ginger wine. The whisky is expected to be a Scotch whisky, usually a blended type.

White Lady.title: White lady (cocktail)
White Lady.text: White lady is a classic cocktail that is made with gin, Cointreau or triple sec, fresh lemon juice and an optional egg white. It belongs to the sidecar family, made with gin in place of brandy.

White Russian.title: White Russian (cocktail)
White Russian.desc: Cocktail made with vodka and coffee liqueur
White Russian.text: A white Russian is a cocktail made with vodka, coffee liqueur and cream served with ice in an old fashioned glass.

White Wine Sangria.title: Sangria
White Wine Sangria.text: Sangria is an alcoholic beverage originating in Spain and Portugal. A punch, sangria traditionally consists of red wine and chopped fruit, often with other ingredients or spirits.

Yellow Bird.title: Yellow bird (cocktail)
Yellow Bird.text: Yellow bird is a Caribbean cocktail.

Zombie.title: Zombie (cocktail)
Zombie.desc: Cocktail made of fruit juices and rum
Zombie.text: The zombie is a tiki cocktail made of fruit juices, liqueurs, and various rums. It first appeared in late 1934, invented by Donn Beach at his Hollywood Don the Beachcomber restaurant.

albarino.title: Albariño
albarino.text: Albariño or Alvarinho is a variety of white wine grape grown in Galicia and in Northwest Portugal where it is also used to make varietal white wines. Albariño is the name for the grape in Galician.

amarone.title: Amarone
amarone.text: Amarone della Valpolicella, usually known as Amarone, is an Italian DOCG denomination of typically rich dry red wine made from the partially dried grapes of the Corvina, Rondinella (5–30%) and other approved red grape varieties.

amontillado.title: Amontillado
amontillado.text: Amontillado is a variety of sherry wine characterised by being darker than fino sherry, but lighter than oloroso sherry.

assyrtiko.title: Assyrtiko
assyrtiko.text: Assyrtiko or Asyrtiko is a white Greek wine grape indigenous to the island of Santorini. Assyrtiko is widely planted in the arid volcanic-ash-rich soil of Santorini and other Aegean islands, such as Paros.

barbera.title: Barbera
barbera.text: Barbera is a red Italian wine grape variety that, as of 2000, was the third most-planted red grape variety in Italy. It produces good yields and is known for deep color, full body, low tannins and high levels of acidity.

barolo.title: Barolo
barolo.text: Barolo is a red denominazione di origine controllata e garantita (DOCG) wine produced in the northern Italian region of Piedmont. It is made from the nebbiolo grape and is often described as one of Italy's greatest wines.

beaujolais.title: Beaujolais
beaujolais.desc: Wine from the Beaujolais region of France
beaujolais.text: Beaujolais is a French appellation d'origine contrôlée (AOC) wine in the Burgundy region. Red Beaujolais wines are generally made of the Gamay grape, which has a thin skin and is low in tannin, but like most AOC wines they are not labeled varietally.

bordeaux.title: Bordeaux wine
bordeaux.desc: Wine produced in the Bordeaux region of France
bordeaux.text: Bordeaux wine is produced in the Bordeaux region of southwest France, around the city of Bordeaux, on the Garonne River.

cab-napa.title: Cabernet Sauvignon
cab-napa.text: Cabernet Sauvignon is one of the world's most widely recognized red wine grape varieties. It is grown in nearly every major wine producing country among a diverse spectrum of climates from Australia and British Columbia, Canada to Lebanon's Beqaa Valley.

cava.title: Cava (Spanish wine)
cava.text: Cava is a sparkling wine of denominación de origen (DO) status from Spain. It may be white (blanco) or rosé (rosado).

chablis.title: Chablis (AOC)
chablis.text: Chablis is the northernmost Appellation d'origine contrôlée of the Burgundy region in France. Its cool climate produces wines with more acidity and less fruitiness than warmer regions growing Chardonnay vines.

champagne.title: Champagne
champagne.text: Champagne is a sparkling wine originated and produced in the Champagne wine region of France under the AOC rules of the appellation, which demand specific vineyard practices, sourcing of grapes exclusively from designated places within it, specific grape-pressing methods and secondary fermentation…

chardonnay-oaked.title: Chardonnay
chardonnay-oaked.desc: Variety of grape mainly used to make wine
chardonnay-oaked.text: Chardonnay is a green-skinned grape variety used in the production of white wine. The variety originated in the Burgundy wine region of east-central France, but is now grown wherever wine is produced, from England to New Zealand.

chenin-blanc.title: Chenin blanc
chenin-blanc.text: Chenin blanc is a white wine grape variety from the Loire Valley of France. Its high acidity means it can be used to make varieties from sparkling wines to well-balanced dessert wines, although it can produce very bland, neutral wines if the vine's natural vigor is not controlled.

chianti.title: Chianti
chianti.text: Chianti is an Italian red wine produced in the Chianti region of central Tuscany, principally from the Sangiovese grape. It was historically associated with a squat bottle enclosed in a straw basket, called a fiasco.

chinon.title: Chinon AOC
chinon.text: Chinon wine comes from the vineyards around the town of Chinon in Touraine. Unusually for the Loire Valley, it is mostly red wine, with 2–5% rosé and a little white wine.

cotes-du-rhone.title: Côtes du Rhône AOC
cotes-du-rhone.text: Côtes du Rhône is a wine-growing Appellation d'Origine Contrôlée (AOC) for the Rhône wine region of France, which may be used throughout the region, also in those areas which are covered by other AOCs.

fino-sherry.title: Fino
fino-sherry.text: Fino is the driest and palest of the traditional varieties of sherry and Montilla-Moriles fortified wine. They are consumed comparatively young and, unlike the sweeter varieties, should be consumed soon after the bottle is opened as exposure to air can cause them to lose their flavour within hours.

gewurztraminer.title: Gewürztraminer
gewurztraminer.text: Gewürztraminer is an aromatic wine grape variety, used in white wines, and which performs best in cooler climates. In English, it is sometimes referred to colloquially as Gewürz.

gruner.title: Grüner Veltliner
gruner.text: Grüner Veltliner German: [ˈɡʁyːnɐ fɛltˈliːnɐ] ) is a white wine grape variety grown primarily in Austria, Hungary, Slovakia, and the Czech Republic.

lambrusco.title: Lambrusco
lambrusco.text: Lambrusco is the name of both an Italian red wine grape and a wine made principally from the grape. The grapes and the wine originate from four zones in Emilia-Romagna and one in Lombardy―principally around the central provinces of Modena, Parma, Reggio-Emilia, and Mantua.

madeira.title: Madeira wine
madeira.desc: Fortified wine made in Madeira, Portugal
madeira.text: Madeira is a fortified wine made on the Portuguese island of Madeira, in the North Atlantic Ocean, just under 400 kilometres (250 mi) north of the Canary Islands, Spain and 520 kilometres (320 mi) west of Morocco.

malbec.title: Malbec
malbec.text: Malbec is a purple grape variety used in making red wine. The grapes tend to have an inky dark color and robust tannins, and are known as one of the six grapes allowed in the blend of red Bordeaux wine.

merlot.title: Merlot
merlot.text: Merlot is a dark-blue-colored wine grape variety that is used as both a blending grape and for varietal wines. The name Merlot is thought to be a diminutive of merle, the French name for the blackbird, probably a reference to the color of the grape.

montepulciano.title: Montepulciano d'Abruzzo
montepulciano.text: Montepulciano d'Abruzzo is an Italian red wine made from the Montepulciano wine grape in the Abruzzo region of east-central Italy. It should not be confused with Vino Nobile di Montepulciano, a Tuscan wine made from Sangiovese and other grapes.

moscato-dasti.title: Moscato d'Asti
moscato-dasti.text: Moscato d'Asti is a denominazione di origine controllata e garantita (DOCG) sparkling white wine made from the Moscato bianco grape and produced mainly in the province of Asti, northwest Italy, and in smaller nearby regions in the provinces of Alessandria and Cuneo.

muscadet.title: Muscadet
muscadet.text: Muscadet is a French white wine. It's made in the Pays nantais, at the western end of the Loire Valley, in the historical region of Brittany.

nz-sauvignon.title: Sauvignon blanc
nz-sauvignon.text: Sauvignon blanc is a green-skinned grape variety that most likely originated in the Loire Valley wine region in France, though it has also been historically cultivated in Bordeaux.

pinot-grigio.title: Pinot gris
pinot-grigio.text: Pinot gris, pinot grigio, or Grauburgunder is a white wine grape variety of the species Vitis vinifera. Thought to be a mutant clone of the pinot noir variety, it normally has a pinkish-gray hue, accounting for its name, but the colors can vary from blue-gray to pinkish-brown.

pinot-noir-nw.title: Pinot noir
pinot-noir-nw.text: Pinot noir, also known as Pinot nero, and Spätburgunder is a red-wine grape variety of the species Vitis vinifera. The name also refers to wines created predominantly from Pinot noir grapes.

prosecco.title: Prosecco
prosecco.text: Prosecco is an Italian DOC or DOCG white wine produced in a large area spanning nine provinces in the Veneto and Friuli-Venezia Giulia regions, and named after the village of Prosecco, in the province of Trieste, Italy.

provence-rose.title: Provence wine
provence-rose.text: Provence wine or Provençal wine comes from the French wine-producing region of Provence in southeast France. The Romans called the area provincia nostra, giving the region its name.

red-burgundy.title: Burgundy wine
red-burgundy.desc: Wine made in the Burgundy region in east-central France
red-burgundy.text: Burgundy wine is a wine made in the Burgundy region of east-central France, in the valleys and slopes west of the Saône, a tributary of the Rhône.

rhone-white.title: Rhône wine
rhone-white.text: The Rhône wine region in Southern France is situated in the Rhône valley and produces numerous wines under various Appellation d'origine contrôlée (AOC) designations. The region's major appellation in production volume is Côtes du Rhône AOC.

riesling-dry.title: Riesling
riesling-dry.text: Riesling is a white grape variety that is believed to have originated from the Rhine Valley region of western Germany, before later being traced to the Alsace region by 1470 and Austria by 1700. Riesling is an aromatic grape variety displaying flowery, almost perfumed aromas as well as high acidity.

riesling-offdry.title: Riesling
riesling-offdry.text: Riesling is a white grape variety that is believed to have originated from the Rhine Valley region of western Germany, before later being traced to the Alsace region by 1470 and Austria by 1700. Riesling is an aromatic grape variety displaying flowery, almost perfumed aromas as well as high acidity.

rioja.title: Rioja DOCa
rioja.text: Rioja is a wine region in Spain, with denominación de origen calificada. Rioja wine is made from grapes grown in the autonomous communities of La Rioja and Navarre, and the Basque province of Álava.

rosado.title: Tavel AOC
rosado.text: Tavel is a wine-growing Appellation d'Origine Contrôlée in the southern Rhône wine region of France, across the Rhône River from Châteauneuf-du-Pape AOC and just north of Avignon. Tavel wines are all rosé wines and must have a minimum alcohol content of 11%.

ruby-port.title: Port wine
ruby-port.text: Port wine, or simply port, is a Portuguese fortified wine produced in the Douro Valley of northern Portugal. It is typically a sweet red wine, often served with dessert, although it also comes in dry, semi-dry, and white varieties.

sancerre.title: Sancerre (wine)
sancerre.desc: French wine from the Loire Valley
sancerre.text: Sancerre is a French wine Appellation d'origine contrôlée (AOC) for wine produced in the area of Sancerre in the eastern part of the Loire valley, southeast of Orléans.

sauternes.title: Sauternes (wine)
sauternes.text: Sauternes is a French sweet wine from the region of the same name in the Graves section in Bordeaux. Sauternes wine is made from Sémillon, sauvignon blanc, and muscadelle grapes that have been affected by Botrytis cinerea, also known as noble rot.

shiraz.title: Syrah
shiraz.text: Syrah, also known as Shiraz, is a dark-skinned grape variety grown throughout the world and used primarily to produce red wine. In 1999, Syrah was found to be the offspring of two obscure grapes from southeastern France, Dureza and Mondeuse Blanche.

syrah-rhone.title: Syrah
syrah-rhone.text: Syrah, also known as Shiraz, is a dark-skinned grape variety grown throughout the world and used primarily to produce red wine. In 1999, Syrah was found to be the offspring of two obscure grapes from southeastern France, Dureza and Mondeuse Blanche.

tawny-port.title: Port wine
tawny-port.text: Port wine, or simply port, is a Portuguese fortified wine produced in the Douro Valley of northern Portugal. It is typically a sweet red wine, often served with dessert, although it also comes in dry, semi-dry, and white varieties.

tokaji.title: Tokaji
tokaji.desc: Hungarian and Slovak variety of wine
tokaji.text: Tokaji or Tokay is a rich, sweet wine originating in the Tokaj wine region in Hungary and in Slovakia. This region is noted for its sweet wines made from grapes affected by noble rot, a style of wine which has a long history in this region.

valpolicella.title: Valpolicella
valpolicella.desc: Valley and wine region in Verona, Italy
valpolicella.text: Valpolicella is a viticultural zone of the province of Verona, Italy, east of Lake Garda. The hilly agricultural and marble-quarrying region of small holdings north of the Adige is famous for wine production.

vermentino.title: Vermentino
vermentino.text: Vermentino is a light-skinned wine grape variety used primarily in Italian wines. It is widely planted in Sardinia, Liguria and Tuscany, to some extent in Corsica, in Piedmont under the name Favorita, and in increasing amounts in Languedoc-Roussillon.

vin-santo.title: Vin Santo
vin-santo.text: Vin Santo is a style of Italian dessert wine. Traditional in Tuscany, these wines are often made from white grape varieties such as Trebbiano and Malvasia, although Sangiovese may be used to produce a rosé style known as "Occhio di Pernice" or eye of the partridge.

vinho-verde.title: Vinho Verde
vinho-verde.text: Vinho Verde is a young Portuguese wine from the DOC "Vinho Verde" region in the far north of Portugal, which includes the original 1908 Minho Province plus adjacent areas to the south.

viognier.title: Viognier
viognier.desc: Variety of grape used to make white wine
viognier.text: Viognier is a white wine grape variety. It is the only permitted grape for the French wine Condrieu in the Rhône Valley.

white-burgundy.title: Burgundy wine
white-burgundy.desc: Wine made in the Burgundy region in east-central France
white-burgundy.text: Burgundy wine is a wine made in the Burgundy region of east-central France, in the valleys and slopes west of the Saône, a tributary of the Rhône.

zinfandel.title: Zinfandel
zinfandel.text: Zinfandel is a variety of black-skinned wine grape. The variety is grown in over 10 percent of California vineyards.
